findings.title: READ issued to a bank one cycle after that bank was PRECHARGEd (no ACTIVATE between)
findings.requirement: After PRE to bank b, no RD/WR to b until an ACT to b (JESD79-3 bank state machine).
findings.expected: After PRE to bank b, no RD/WR to b until an ACT to b (JESD79-3 bank state machine).
findings.actual: PRE b=1 at cycle 183, RD b=1 at cycle 184.
findings.mechanism: JasperGold counterexample, 136 cycles from reset under a protocol-legal host: cycle 183 PRE bank 1 (A10=0), cycle 184 RD bank 1 col 0. The generated PROTO_001 tracker (row-open state from the observed ACT/PRE stream) shows bank 1 closed when the READ is issued. Never observed in simulation (no path stimulus reaches this interleaving); the scheduler or its bank_tracker gating lets a CAS follow its own precharge. Likely the same root as the open scheduler re-grant defect (commands are also held for 2-3 consecutive cycles in the trace, i.e. re-issued). [found on drop 1fea117; awaiting formal re-prove on 43f6cb8f0641]

findings.title: PRECHARGE issued one cycle after a WRITE to the same bank (tWR violated; write data lost)
findings.requirement: WR to bank b then no PRE to b for tWR (2 free cycles at 5 ns).
findings.expected: WR to bank b then no PRE to b for tWR (2 free cycles at 5 ns).
findings.actual: WR b=4 at cycle 173, PRE b=4 at cycle 174.
findings.mechanism: JasperGold counterexample, 136 cycles from reset under a protocol-legal host: cycle 173 WR bank 4, cycle 174 PRE bank 4. tWR = 15 ns = 3 controller cycles, so 2 cycles must separate the last write beat from the precharge. Not observed in simulation. bank_tracker's write-recovery timer (cfg_tWR_nCK) does not gate bank_pre_allowed for the cycle after a write, or the scheduler ignores it on the row-conflict path. [found on drop 1fea117; awaiting formal re-prove on 43f6cb8f0641]

findings.title: Write acknowledge and read response complete in the same cycle on the one Wishbone ack line
findings.requirement: One acknowledge per accepted beat (host_interface.interface_type = wishbone_pipelined). When a write acknowledge and a read response are due in the same cycle the port must hold one of them (a one-entry response or write-ack holding register) so each completes in its own cycle.
findings.expected: One acknowledge per accepted beat (host_interface.interface_type = wishbone_pipelined). When a write acknowledge and a read response are due in the same cycle the port must hold one of them (a one-entry response or write-ack holding register) so each completes in its own cycle.
findings.actual: cex at bound 24: $past(wb_cyc_i && wb_stb_i && !wb_stall_o && wb_we_i) && rsp_valid is reachable
findings.mechanism: JasperGold counterexample 24 cycles from reset, engine L, no abstraction (cover c_HOST_001, a write beat accepted, reached at cycle 1). wb_port.sv: wr_ack_r <= wb_beat & wb_we_i (the write acknowledge, one cycle after the beat) and assign wb_ack_o = wr_ack_r | rd_ack with rd_ack = rsp_valid. A read response arriving the cycle after a write beat is accepted gives one wb_ack_o pulse for two completions; the host counts one acknowledge, waits for the other forever (a pipelined master) or mis-attributes the read data to the write (a classic one). Any legal host reaches it: issue a read, then present a write beat the cycle before the read data returns. Not seen in simulation on 2026-10-28 only because no sequence placed a write beat on that cycle (243 pipelined beats on path_07). SIMULATION WITNESS (2026-10-29, path_23_host_ack_collision, ack_collision.py): a read to an open row and a write beat accepted 41 cycles later (gap d = 40) -- the write acknowledge and the read response fall in the same cycle at t = 35.37 us; a_HOST_001 fires once, every request and response is conserved, and the host handshake stage counts 1 of 79 beats never acknowledged: the one ack pulse the two completions shared. [found on drop 99f72da45a32; awaiting formal re-prove on 43f6cb8f0641]
